_summary: Read in full on 2026-10-06: the candidate of #16 (the owner's three fixes: s-firm's products_in_budget with its fixed closing line and two lints, Crypto Fund Trader's fees in firm_rules, the crossover guardrail with no quotable phrase and a lint for the leak), all 30 cases, 40 s apart. 28 of 30 automatically; p-size's automated failure is the checker's, ex-angry's is real. On a read, five errors, one critical. Critical: ex-angry's 'To reconstruct the calculation, we need the inputs' is the first person (run 22's 'Let's'); the same reply states Crypto Fund Trader's and BrightFunded's drawdown types from no tool, undated. Two major: p-crossover's 'below $98,000 at the day's start, the $6,000 max-loss budget would be the smaller one' (below $98,000 the drawdown budget is under $4,000); p-hold's '10 trading days' where the firm's page says 'Every 10 days'. Two minor: p-size repeats the assumptions the service lists; s-product names size_trade and check_budget. s-firm right: all five products cheapest first, the fixed line, no product picked, the model's own words. No quoted phrase from the instructions in any reply. q-stats gives out of sample first; ex-recovery keeps to every maximum loss troid has read.

p-crossover: Error (rule): $98,000 first, quota × (1 − max% + daily%), the $96,000 and $94,000 floors and the $4,000 and $6,000 budgets on a $100,000 day, which one binds turning on the day's start alone ('however much was lost or clawed back earlier'), no quoted phrase; but 'below $98,000 at the day's start, the $6,000 max-loss budget would be the smaller one' is wrong: below $98,000 the drawdown budget is under $4,000; $6,000 is its size on a $100,000 day. Today's five p-crossover runs before it were right.
